subject: SCI
title: Science 3
description: A hands-on, NGSS-aligned third-grade science course covering forces and motion, magnets and static electricity, life cycles, animal groups, inheritance and variation, fossils, habitats and environmental change, weather and climate, and weather-related hazards. Students conduct investigations with household materials, keep a science notebook, construct evidence-based arguments, and complete engineering design challenges.
framework: California Next Generation Science Standards (CA NGSS); 2016 CA Science Framework

standards.3-PS2-1: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence of the effects of balanced and unbalanced forces on the motion of an object.
standards.3-PS2-2: Make observations and/or measurements of an object's motion to provide evidence that a pattern can be used to predict future motion.
standards.3-PS2-3: Ask questions to determine cause and effect relationships of electric or magnetic interactions between two objects not in contact with each other.
standards.3-PS2-4: Define a simple design problem that can be solved by applying scientific ideas about magnets.
standards.3-LS1-1: Develop models to describe that organisms have unique and diverse life cycles but all have in common birth, growth, reproduction and death.
standards.3-LS2-1: Construct an argument that some animals form groups that help members survive.
standards.3-LS3-1: Analyze and interpret data to provide evidence that plants and animals have traits inherited from parents and that variation of these traits exists in a group of similar organisms.
standards.3-LS3-2: Use evidence to support the explanation that traits can be influenced by the environment.
standards.3-LS4-1: Analyze and interpret data from fossils to provide evidence of the organisms and the environments in which they lived long ago.
standards.3-LS4-2: Use evidence to construct an explanation for how variations in characteristics among individuals of the same species may provide advantages in surviving, finding mates and reproducing.
standards.3-LS4-3: Construct an argument with evidence that in a particular habitat some organisms can survive well, some survive less well, and some cannot survive at all.
standards.3-LS4-4: Make a claim about the merit of a solution to a problem caused when the environment changes and the types of plants and animals that live there may change.
standards.3-ESS2-1: Represent data in tables and graphical displays to describe typical weather conditions expected during a particular season.
standards.3-ESS2-2: Obtain and combine information to describe climates in different regions of the world.
standards.3-ESS3-1: Make a claim about the merit of a design solution that reduces the impacts of a weather-related hazard.
standards.3-5-ETS1-1: Define a simple design problem reflecting a need or want that includes specified criteria for success and constraints on materials, time or cost.
standards.3-5-ETS1-2: Generate and compare multiple possible solutions to a problem based on how well each is likely to meet the criteria and constraints.
standards.3-5-ETS1-3: Plan and carry out fair tests in which variables are controlled and failure points are considered to identify aspects of a model or prototype that can be improved.

resources.note: Free grade 3 mystery videos and hands-on activities on forces, life cycles, fossils and weather

resources.name: PBS LearningMedia
resources.note: Free videos and interactives searchable by grade and NGSS standard

resources.name: NASA Climate Kids
resources.note: Weather, climate and Earth science articles and games for kids

resources.name: NOAA SciJinks
resources.note: Kid-friendly weather explanations, hazard guides and activities

resources.name: PhET Interactive Simulations

resources.name: Smithsonian Learning Lab
resources.note: Fossil, animal and natural history images and collections from the Smithsonian

units.title: Forces and Motion
units.big_idea: Pushes and pulls change motion when forces are unbalanced, and patterns of motion can be predicted.

units.title: Magnets and Static Electricity
units.big_idea: Some forces act at a distance; we can use magnets to solve problems.

units.title: Life Cycles
units.big_idea: All living things are born, grow, reproduce and die, but their life cycles differ.

units.title: Animal Groups and Survival
units.big_idea: Living in groups helps some animals survive.

units.title: Inheritance, Variation and Environment
units.big_idea: Offspring inherit traits from parents, traits vary, and environment can influence traits.

units.title: Fossils and Past Environments
units.big_idea: Fossils are evidence of organisms and environments from long ago.

units.title: Habitats and Environmental Change
units.big_idea: Organisms survive best in habitats that meet their needs; when environments change, solutions can help.

units.title: Weather and Climate
units.big_idea: Weather follows seasonal patterns that can be measured, and climates differ around the world.

units.title: Natural Hazards and Engineering Design
units.big_idea: Engineers design solutions that reduce the impacts of weather-related hazards.

objectives: Identify forces as pushes and pulls

days.title: Forces around us
days.work: List 20 pushes and pulls seen at home and sort them in a science notebook T-chart.

days.title: Tug of war
days.work: Play a gentle towel tug-of-war with a family member and draw force arrows for balanced and unbalanced pulls.

days.title: Book stack
days.work: Push a book with equal force from both sides, then unequal force, and record what happens to its motion.

days.title: Video and model
days.work: Watch a Mystery Science forces lesson and draw arrow diagrams for a stationary and a moving object.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain in writing with diagrams why an object starts moving only when forces are unbalanced.

objectives: Plan a fair test of force on motion

days.title: Plan a test
days.work: Plan a fair test: does ramp height change how far a toy car travels? Identify what stays the same.

days.title: Ramp investigation
days.work: Run 3 trials at each of 3 ramp heights and record distances in a data table.

days.title: Friction test
days.work: Roll the car down the same ramp onto carpet, tile and towel and measure distances.

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Graph results and write a claim about force, friction and motion supported by data.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain how you kept the test fair and what you would improve.

weeks.assessment: Lab report with data table and claim

objectives: Use patterns to predict future motion

days.title: Pendulum build
days.work: Build a pendulum from string and washers and count swings in 15 seconds.

days.title: Change length
days.work: Change the string length and record the pattern in swing count; predict the next result.

days.title: Bouncing ball
days.work: Drop a ball and measure bounce heights; describe the pattern of decreasing bounces.

days.title: Playground patterns
days.work: Observe a swing or seesaw and describe repeating motion patterns.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Use your pendulum data to predict swings for a new length, then test the prediction.

objectives: Apply force concepts to a design

days.title: Marble run plan
days.work: Plan a cardboard marble run that makes a marble travel 1 meter and stop in a cup.

days.title: Build
days.work: Build the marble run using tape and cardboard tubes.

days.title: Test
days.work: Test and record where the marble fails; identify the force causing each failure.

days.title: Improve
days.work: Modify the design and retest, recording changes.

days.title: Unit 1 assessment
days.work: Complete the unit quiz on balanced/unbalanced forces and motion patterns.

weeks.assessment: Unit 1 quiz; marble run testing log

days.title: Magnet hunt
days.work: Test 15 household objects with a magnet and sort into attracted / not attracted.

days.title: Poles
days.work: Explore north and south poles and record which combinations attract or repel.

days.title: Through materials
days.work: Test whether magnetic force works through paper, cardboard, water and plastic.

days.title: Distance
days.work: Measure how far a paper clip can be from a magnet before it is pulled, using different numbers of paper sheets.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write cause-and-effect sentences explaining magnetic interactions.

days.title: Balloon charge
days.work: Rub a balloon on hair and test whether it attracts tissue paper bits.

days.title: Rolling can
days.work: Use a charged balloon to roll an empty aluminum can without touching it.

days.title: Two balloons
days.work: Charge two balloons and observe repulsion; record observations.

days.title: Simulation
days.work: Explore the PhET 'Balloons and Static Electricity' simulation and draw charges.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write 3 testable cause-and-effect questions about static electricity and answer one.

objectives: Define a design problem solvable with magnets

days.title: Define a problem
days.work: Define a problem (keeping a cabinet door closed or finding lost pins) with criteria and constraints.

days.title: Brainstorm
days.work: Sketch 3 possible magnet solutions and compare them against the criteria.

days.title: Build
days.work: Build the best solution prototype.

days.title: Test
days.work: Test and evaluate the prototype; record what worked.

days.title: Unit 2 assessment
days.work: Present the design and complete the unit quiz on magnets and static electricity.

objectives: Model the life cycle of a flowering plant

days.title: Germination bag
days.work: Plant beans in wet paper towels in a zip bag and tape to a window; predict what will happen.

days.title: Seed dissection
days.work: Soak a bean and open it to find the seed coat, embryo and food supply; draw and label.

days.title: Flower parts
days.work: Dissect a flower from the garden or store and identify parts used for reproduction.

days.title: Measure growth
days.work: Measure and record bean sprout growth and draw daily observations.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw a circular model of a flowering plant's life cycle with labels.

materials: pictures or video of butterflies and grasshoppers

days.title: Butterfly
days.work: Watch a butterfly metamorphosis video and sequence egg, larva, pupa, adult cards.

days.title: Grasshopper
days.work: Compare grasshopper incomplete metamorphosis to the butterfly in a Venn diagram.

days.title: Clay models
days.work: Build clay models of each stage of a ladybug life cycle.

days.title: Bean check
days.work: Measure and graph bean plant growth so far.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain in writing what all insect life cycles have in common.

weeks.topic: Animal life cycles: frogs, birds, mammals
objectives: Identify birth, growth, reproduction, death in all

days.title: Frogs
days.work: Sequence the frog life cycle and describe changes from tadpole to adult.

days.title: Birds
days.work: Examine an egg (shell, membrane, yolk) and diagram a chicken's life cycle.

days.title: Mammals
days.work: Compare a human and a dog life cycle using a timeline.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Make a chart comparing life span and stages of 5 organisms.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer questions about which stages all life cycles share.

objectives: Develop and present a life cycle model

days.title: Choose an organism
days.work: Research a chosen organism's life cycle (sea turtle, salmon, oak tree).

days.title: Build model
days.work: Build a spinning paper-plate life cycle model.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the model and explain each stage.

days.title: Bean wrap-up
days.work: Transplant bean sprouts to soil and describe the next stages expected.

days.title: Unit 3 assessment
days.work: Complete the unit quiz on life cycles.

objectives: Identify ways group living helps animals survive
Gather evidence from texts and video

days.title: Group examples
days.work: Watch videos of wolf packs, fish schools and bee colonies and list benefits.

days.title: Ant observation
days.work: Observe ants outdoors (or a video) and record how they work together.

days.title: Evidence chart
days.work: Read articles and fill an evidence chart: hunting, defense, raising young, staying warm.

days.title: Fish school model
days.work: Model a fish school vs. a lone fish in a predator tag game and record results.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Summarize evidence for one animal group.

days.title: Claim
days.work: Write a claim: living in groups helps [animal] survive.

days.title: Evidence
days.work: Choose 3 pieces of evidence from the evidence chart.

days.title: Reasoning
days.work: Explain how each piece of evidence supports the claim.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the argument and answer questions.

days.title: Unit 4 assessment
days.work: Complete the unit quiz on animal groups.

days.title: Trait sort
days.work: Sort animal parent and offspring pictures and identify inherited traits.

days.title: Family traits
days.work: Survey family members for traits (earlobes, tongue rolling, hair color) and record data.

days.title: Plants inherit
days.work: Compare seeds from one plant to offspring plants.

days.title: Graph
days.work: Graph survey data on traits.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain what inherited traits are using examples.

objectives: Observe and measure variation within a species
materials: peanuts in shells or leaves from one tree

days.title: Peanut variation
days.work: Measure 20 peanut shells and record lengths.

days.title: Line plot
days.work: Make a line plot of the lengths and describe the variation.

days.title: Leaf variation
days.work: Collect 15 leaves from one tree and compare size, shape and color.

days.title: Dogs
days.work: Compare different dog breeds and discuss variation within a species.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a conclusion about variation with evidence from your data.

objectives: Gather evidence that environment influences traits

days.title: Plant experiment setup
days.work: Place one plant in sunlight and one in a dark closet; predict differences.

days.title: Examples
days.work: Read about flamingos' color from diet and hydrangea color from soil.

days.title: Measure plants
days.work: Measure and observe plants and record height and color.

days.title: Human examples
days.work: Discuss how exercise and diet can influence traits.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write evidence that environment influences traits from the plant experiment.

objectives: Explain how variation may provide advantages for survival

days.title: Camouflage game
days.work: Scatter colored paper 'insects' on grass and time how many a family member finds; record which colors survive.

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Graph results and explain the advantage of camouflage.

days.title: Other advantages
days.work: Research how longer beaks or thicker fur help individuals survive.

days.title: Write
days.work: Explain how a variation could help an animal find a mate or food.

days.title: Unit 5 assessment
days.work: Complete the unit quiz on traits and variation.

materials: plaster of Paris or salt dough

days.title: Fossil formation
days.work: Watch a fossil video and sequence the steps of fossil formation.

days.title: Make fossils
days.work: Make imprint fossils by pressing shells into clay; fill with plaster to make casts.

days.title: Fossil types
days.work: Compare body fossils, trace fossils and imprints using Smithsonian images.

days.title: La Brea
days.work: Learn about the La Brea Tar Pits and the animals found there.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain how fossils form in a comic strip.

weeks.topic: Fossils as evidence of past environments
objectives: Analyze fossil data to infer past environments

days.title: Fossil clues
days.work: Examine fossil cards (fish, fern, shark tooth) and infer past environments.

days.title: Rock layers
days.work: Build a layered sandwich model of rock layers and discuss older vs. newer layers.

days.title: Desert ocean
days.work: Investigate why marine fossils are found in deserts and mountains.

days.title: Data table
days.work: Complete a data table matching fossils to environments.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a claim about a past environment using fossil evidence.

objectives: Compare extinct organisms to living ones

days.title: Mammoth and elephant
days.work: Compare a mammoth and an elephant and infer the mammoth's environment.

days.title: Dinosaurs and birds
days.work: Compare dinosaur and bird fossils.

days.title: Research
days.work: Research one extinct organism and its environment.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present a museum card for the organism.

days.title: Unit 6 assessment
days.work: Complete the unit quiz on fossils.

objectives: Describe how habitats meet organisms' needs

days.title: Backyard habitat
days.work: Survey a backyard or park and list organisms and their needs.

days.title: Habitat cards
days.work: Match organisms to habitats (desert, ocean, forest, wetland).

days.title: Survive well, less well
days.work: Sort organisms by how well they would survive in a desert.

days.title: Pill bug choice
days.work: Test whether pill bugs prefer damp or dry soil in a shoebox choice chamber.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an argument for which habitat suits a cactus best.

days.title: Tide pools
days.work: Learn how tide pool animals survive waves and drying out.

days.title: Chaparral
days.work: Study chaparral plants' adaptations to dry summers and fire.

days.title: Redwood forest
days.work: Study redwood forest organisms and fog.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Compare which organisms could survive in each habitat.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an argument with evidence about one organism's survival in a California habitat.

objectives: Describe how environmental change affects organisms

days.title: Changes
days.work: List natural and human-caused environmental changes (drought, fire, building).

days.title: Drought test
days.work: Water one plant and withhold water from another; observe effects.

days.title: Case study
days.work: Read about how the California drought affected salmon.

days.title: Predict
days.work: Predict what happens to organisms when a wetland is drained.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain cause-and-effect of environmental change in writing.

objectives: Evaluate the merit of solutions to environmental change

days.title: Solutions
days.work: Read about wildlife crossings, fish ladders and habitat restoration.

days.title: Evaluate
days.work: Compare 2 solutions for the salmon problem using criteria.

days.title: Claim
days.work: Make a claim about the best solution with evidence.

days.title: Poster
days.work: Create a poster about the chosen solution.

days.title: Unit 7 assessment
days.work: Complete the unit quiz on habitats and environmental change.

objectives: Identify weather conditions and the tools that measure them

days.title: Weather words
days.work: Define temperature, precipitation, wind and cloud cover and set up a daily weather log page in your science notebook.

days.title: Rain gauge
days.work: Build a rain gauge by taping a ruler to a straight-sided jar and place it in an open spot outdoors.

days.title: Wind vane
days.work: Build a wind vane from a straw, index-card arrow and pencil eraser, and mark N/S/E/W with a compass app.

days.title: Thermometer
days.work: Read an outdoor thermometer at 8 a.m., noon and 4 p.m. and explain why temperatures change through the day.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain what each homemade instrument measures and record a full day's weather using all of them.

weeks.assessment: Instrument explanation and first log entries

objectives: Collect and record daily weather data

days.title: Clouds
days.work: Learn cumulus, stratus and cirrus clouds using SciJinks, then identify today's clouds and sketch them in the log.

days.title: Daily data
days.work: Record temperature, rainfall, wind direction and cloud type at the same time each day.

days.title: Forecasts
days.work: Compare your observations to the NOAA/National Weather Service forecast for your town and note matches.

days.title: Data table
days.work: Organize the week's measurements into a data table with units and calculate the week's high and low.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Describe the week's weather pattern in 3 sentences using numbers from your table.

objectives: Describe typical weather for each season

days.title: Local data
days.work: Look up average monthly temperature and rainfall for your city and copy them into a table.

days.title: Rainfall bar graph
days.work: Draw a bar graph of average monthly rainfall with a labeled scale.

days.title: Temperature line graph
days.work: Draw a line graph of average monthly high temperatures.

days.title: Interpret
days.work: Use both graphs to describe the typical weather in winter, spring, summer and fall.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Predict next month's typical weather from the graphs and compare it to your log later.

objectives: Describe climates in different world regions

days.title: Weather vs. climate
days.work: Sort 10 statements as weather (today's rain) or climate (rainy winters every year) and explain the difference.

days.title: Climate zones
days.work: Color a world map by climate zone (polar, temperate, tropical, desert) using a NASA Climate Kids reference.

days.title: Compare cities
days.work: Compare yearly temperature and rainfall for Anchorage, Singapore and Cairo in a table.

days.title: People adapt
days.work: Research how people in one climate region dress, build homes and farm.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a description of one climate region with at least 3 data facts.

objectives: Obtain and combine information to describe climates in California's regions

days.title: CA regions
days.work: Mark the coast, Central Valley, Sierra Nevada and desert regions on a California map.

days.title: City data
days.work: Collect monthly temperature and rainfall for San Diego, Sacramento, South Lake Tahoe and Death Valley.

days.title: Graph and compare
days.work: Graph the 4 cities' July highs and yearly rainfall on bar graphs and compare.

days.title: Travel guide
days.work: Write a one-page travel guide describing one region's climate and what to pack in each season.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Share the travel guide and explain how elevation and the ocean affect California climates.

days.title: Log analysis
days.work: Graph 4 weeks of your own temperature data and find the warmest and coolest days.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Compare your local data to the same weeks in a city with a different climate.

days.title: Vocabulary game
days.work: Play a weather vocabulary matching game with flash cards (precipitation, climate, cirrus, etc.).

days.title: Weather report
days.work: Present a 2-minute TV-style weather report for your city using your data and a map.

days.title: Unit 8 assessment
days.work: Complete the unit test on weather data, seasons and climates.

objectives: Identify weather-related hazards and their impacts on people

days.title: Hazards
days.work: Read SciJinks pages and list 6 weather-related hazards with a sentence describing each.

days.title: California hazards
days.work: Research flooding, drought and wildfire in California, including a recent event.

days.title: Impacts
days.work: Make a chart of each hazard's impacts on people, homes, animals and land.

days.title: Preparation
days.work: Create a family emergency kit checklist and evacuation plan for the hazard most likely where you live.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain in a paragraph how one hazard affects a community and how people prepare.

objectives: Evaluate the merit of design solutions that reduce hazard impacts

days.title: Solutions
days.work: Read about levees, lightning rods, storm shelters and fire breaks and how each reduces damage.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Compare 3 flood solutions in a table by cost, effectiveness and effects on nature.

days.title: Flood model
days.work: Build a sand-and-pan river model, pour water to flood a 'town,' then test a clay levee.

days.title: Claim
days.work: Write a claim about which flood solution has the most merit for a riverside town, with evidence from the model.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present the claim and answer a family member's questions about trade-offs.

weeks.assessment: Claim about hazard solution with model evidence

objectives: Define a design problem with criteria and constraints

days.title: Problem
days.work: Define the challenge: protect a small model house from strong wind and heavy rain.

days.title: Criteria and constraints
days.work: List criteria (stays standing at fan high speed, inside stays dry) and constraints (cardboard, tape, 1 plastic bag, 3 days).

days.title: Research
days.work: Look at how real hurricane-resistant houses use roof straps, shutters and raised foundations.

days.title: Sketch
days.work: Sketch 3 different house designs with labels.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Score each design against the criteria and choose one to build.

days.title: Build
days.work: Build the model house from cardboard and tape following your chosen sketch.

days.title: Wind test
days.work: Test the house in front of a box fan at low, medium and high, keeping distance the same; record failure points.

days.title: Rain test
days.work: Place a dry paper towel inside and spray 30 squirts of water from above; record leaks.

days.title: Improve
days.work: Modify the weakest part of the design based on test results.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Retest the improved house under the same conditions and compare results in a table.

objectives: Improve a design and argue for its merit

days.title: Final test
days.work: Run 3 final wind and rain trials on the improved model and record results.

days.title: Data
days.work: Make a bar graph comparing performance before and after improvements.

days.title: Poster
days.work: Create a poster showing the problem, design, test data and improvements.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the solution and argue how well it meets the criteria and constraints.

days.title: Unit 9 assessment
days.work: Complete the unit quiz on weather hazards and the engineering design process.

days.title: Forces review
days.work: Review forces and magnets with a quick ramp and magnet demo.

days.title: Life science review
days.work: Review life cycles, traits and habitats with a card sort.

days.title: Earth science review
days.work: Review fossils, weather and hazards with a vocabulary game.

days.title: Final assessment
days.work: Complete the end-of-year science assessment.

days.title: Showcase
days.work: Share the science notebook and favorite investigation with family.
